Furthermore, he shall transcend the suffering of birth and death for as many kalpas as there are steps; moreover, in future lives for as many kalpas as there are steps, he shall receive the supreme and distinguished rank of a Wheel-Turning King."
With every step, they shall increase their merit and sovereignty in this present life, with inconceivable spiritual resonance that is revered by all;

for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of kalpas, they shall enjoy the seven precious palaces among humans and devas, always becoming kings wherever they are born, increasing their lifespan, possessing eloquent speech that is trusted and accepted by humans and devas, being free from fear, and attaining great renown; all shall look up to them in reverence as they experience supreme and wondrous bliss among devas and humans, obtaining great power and majesty, with a physical form that is marvelous, upright, and peerless; they shall encounter the Teacher of Devas and Humans, meet with virtuous friends, and fully accomplish an immeasurable accumulation of merit.
"O Four Kings, you should know!
Because those kings of men perceive such various and immeasurable merits and benefits, they ought to go in person to welcome and honor the Dharma Master."
Whether it be one *yojana* or even up to a hundred thousand *yojanas*, one should conceive the thought of a Buddha toward the Dharma-preacher. Having returned to the city, one should reflect thus:
"Today the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni entered my palace, accepted my offerings, and preached the Dharma for me."
Having heard the Dharma, I shall no longer regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; this is equivalent to encountering hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of Buddha-Bhagavāns.
Today, by means of these various vast, supreme, and exquisite articles of enjoyment, I make offerings to all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
"Today, I have forever uprooted the sufferings of the realm of King Yama, of the hells, the hungry ghosts, and the animals.
I have already planted the seeds of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of roots of goodness for becoming a Wheel-Turning Sage King, a Śakra, or a Brahmā Lord."

May immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of sentient beings be delivered from the suffering of birth and death and attain the bliss of nirvāṇa; may they accumulate an immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable mass of merit. May the members of the inner court, the retinue, and all the people receive peace and security; may the land be pure and tranquil, free from all calamities, poison, harm, and wicked men; may enemies from other regions not come to invade or disturb it, and may it remain far removed from sorrow and affliction.

"O Four Kings, you should know that at that time, the king of men shall thus honor the True Dharma, and he shall also offer worship, respect, reverence, and praise to the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who uphold this sublime sūtra. Whatever roots of goodness he thereby acquires, he shall first bestow those supreme merits upon you and your retinues."

That king, by virtue of the causes and conditions of his great merit and virtuous karma, shall attain great sovereignty and increased majesty in this present life; he will be adorned with all auspicious and wondrous marks, and he will be able to subdue all enemies through the True Dharma.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there is a king who can thus show reverence for the True Dharma, listen to this King of Sutras, and furthermore, respectfully make offerings to, revere, and praise those among the fourfold assembly who uphold this sutra.”

At that time, desiring to bring us joy, that king of men shall stand to one side near the Dharma-seat; having sprinkled the ground with scented water and scattered various famous flowers, he shall prepare a place and set out four lion-thrones, so that I and that king may together listen to the True Dharma.
May the king’s own roots of goodness for his self-benefit also be shared with us as a portion of his merit.
World-Honored One!
When that king of men invites the Dharma-preacher to ascend the seat, he shall burn various famous incenses for our sake and make offerings to this sutra.
World-Honored One!
At that moment, the fragrant smoke rose into the void in a single thought-instant and immediately reached the celestial palaces of us gods, where it transformed in mid-air into a canopy of incense.

When we, the hosts of devas, smelled that exquisite fragrance, its golden light illuminated the palaces where we dwell, extending even to the Brahma-heavens, as well as the abodes of Śakra, Mahāprajñaptī-devī, Mahāśrī-devī, the Earth Goddess Dhṛtarāṣṭrā, the General Vijñānakāya, the yakṣa spirits of the twenty-eight divisions, Maheśvara, Vajrapāṇi, the General Ratnapāla, Hārītī with her five hundred retinues, the Naga King Anavatapta, and the Naga King of the Great Ocean.
“World-Honored One!

These various assemblies, within their own palaces, saw that incense smoke which, in a single kṣaṇa, transformed into a canopy of fragrance. They smelled its exquisite scent and beheld its radiant colors as it pervaded all the celestial palaces of the gods.”
The Buddha addressed the Four Heavenly Kings:
"This fragrant light did not merely reach this palace and transform into a fragrant canopy emitting great radiance;

rather, because that human king held a censer in his hand and burned various famous incenses as an offering while the sutra was being recited, the fragrance and smoke reached throughout the trichiliocosm in a single thought-moment. It filled and remained in the void within the palaces of all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas throughout the ten billion suns and moons, the ten billion Sumeru Kings, and the ten billion four-continent worlds of this trichiliocosm."
Various kinds of incense smoke transformed into canopies of clouds, and these golden canopies shone everywhere throughout the celestial palaces.
Thus, all the various fragrant clouds and fragrant canopies throughout this trichiliocosm are due to the majestic spiritual power of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, the Sovereign King of Sutras.

When these kings of men hold incense burners to make offerings during the recitation of the sutra, the various fragrances not only pervade this trichiliocosm, but in a single thought-moment, they also pervade hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of Buddha-lands as numerous as the sands of immeasurable and boundless Ganges Rivers throughout the ten directions. Above the Buddhas, in the midst of the void, these fragrances transform into canopies of incense, and their golden light shines everywhere in the same manner.

At that time, those Buddhas, having heard this sublime fragrance and beheld these canopies of clouds as well as the golden light, manifested spiritual transformations throughout worlds in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Then, all those World-Honored Ones gazed upon one another and, with one voice and in unison, praised the Dharma Master, saying:
"Excellent!"
Excellent! You,
Great Being, who are able to widely disseminate such a profound and subtle sutra, shall thereby accomplish an immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable accumulation of merit and virtue.

If there are those who hear such a sutra as this, the measure of the merit they obtain is exceedingly great; how much more so for those who copy it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, expound it for others, and practice according to its teachings.
Why is this? Good son!
If there are sentient beings who hear this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, they shall no longer regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, from hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of immeasurable and innumerable Buddha-fields in the ten directions—equal in number to the sands of the Ganges—all the Tathāgatas in those fields, with one voice and in unison, praised that Dharma-preacher from their seats, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
Excellent, son of good family!

In a future age, through the power of your diligent effort, you shall practice immeasurable hundreds of thousands of ascetic austerities and perfect the provisions for enlightenment. You shall surpass all the assembly of noble ones, transcend the three realms, and become the most supreme Honored One. Seated beneath the king of bodhi trees, adorned with sublime splendor, you shall be able to rescue sentient beings with karmic affinities throughout the trichiliocosm; you shall skillfully subdue the hosts of Māra’s armies with their terrifying forms and appearances, and awaken to the most supreme, pure, profound, and unsurpassed right and equal enlightenment of all dharmas.
"Son of good family!

You shall sit upon the diamond throne and turn the supreme, profound wheel of Dharma of the twelve sublime practices praised by all Buddhas; you shall be able to beat the unsurpassed, greatest drum of Dharma, blow the unsurpassed, most exquisite conch of Dharma, raise the unsurpassed, most excellent banner of Dharma, kindle the unsurpassed, most brilliant torch of Dharma, and rain down the unsurpassed nectar of Dharma. You shall sever the immeasurable knots of afflictions and enmity, enable immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of sentient beings to cross the shoreless and fearsome great ocean, liberate them from the boundless cycle of birth and death, and cause them to encounter immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of Buddhas."
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, the King of Sutras, is able to accomplish such immeasurable merits in the future and the present. Therefore, if a king of men should hear this subtle and wondrous scripture, he has already planted roots of goodness before hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of immeasurable Buddhas; we shall protect and keep such a king of men in mind.”

Furthermore, because we behold immeasurable merit and benefit, we—the four kings and our retinues of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of deities—shall, at the time of witnessing these various miraculous transformations of fragrant smoke, cloud-canopies, and divine manifestations within our own palaces, conceal ourselves and remain invisible. For the sake of hearing the Dharma, we shall proceed to the place where this king’s pure and magnificently adorned palace stands, to the location where the Dharma is being preached.

In this manner, even as far as the Brahma palaces, Śakra, Mahāprajñāpāramitā-devī, Mahāśrī-devī, the Earth Goddess Dṛḍhā, the General Suvijñāpakasamjñaka, the yakṣa spirits of the twenty-eight divisions, Maheśvara, Vajrapāṇi, the General Ratnapāla, Hārītī with her five hundred retinues, the Naga King Anavatapta, the Naga King of the Great Ocean, and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of devas and yakṣas—all these multitudes, for the sake of hearing the Dharma, remained invisible and proceeded to that place where the human king’s magnificent palace was adorned and the high seat for preaching the Dharma was set.
"Blessed One!

We, the four kings and our retinues—the yakṣas and various deities—all shall with one mind act as spiritual friends to those human kings. Because they are donors of this unsurpassed great Dharma, we have been satisfied by them with the flavor of ambrosia; therefore, we shall protect these kings, eliminate their misfortunes and afflictions, and cause them to attain peace and security. Furthermore, all evil calamities and transformations within their palaces, cities, towns, and kingdoms shall be entirely extinguished."
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings joined their palms together and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there is a king of men within his realm who, although this sutra exists, does not cause it to circulate, but instead gives rise to thoughts of abandonment, takes no pleasure in hearing it, and neither makes offerings to, respects, nor praises it; and if, seeing members of the fourfold assembly who uphold this sutra, he likewise fails to respect or make offerings to them—this will ultimately cause us and our immeasurable celestial retinues to be unable to hear this profound and wondrous Dharma. We shall turn our backs on the flavor of the nectar, lose the stream of the True Dharma, lack majestic radiance and power, increase the realms of evil destinies, diminish the worlds of humans and devas, fall into the river of birth and death, and stray from the path to Nirvana.”
"World-Honored One!
We four kings, together with our retinues and yakṣas, seeing such matters as these, shall abandon those lands and have no heart for protection."
Not only have we abandoned this king, but all the immeasurable great benevolent deities who protect the land have likewise departed.

Once these have been abandoned, that kingdom shall suffer various calamities and lose its sovereignty; all the people will lack a virtuous heart, being characterized only by bondage, killing, hatred, and strife, slandering one another and falsely implicating the innocent. Epidemics will spread, comets will appear frequently, two suns will manifest simultaneously, eclipses will occur without constancy, and black and white rainbows will portend signs of misfortune. Shooting stars and earthquakes will occur, wells will emit sounds, and violent rains and fierce winds will arise out of season. The land will constantly suffer from famine, crops will fail to ripen, and foreign enemies and bandits will frequently invade and plunder. The people within the realm will endure manifold sufferings, and there will be no place in the land that is pleasant.
"Bhagavān!

When we four kings, together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devas, as well as the long-standing benevolent deities who protect the land, depart and withdraw, such immeasurable hundreds of thousands of calamitous and malevolent events will arise."
World-Honored One!

If there is a king who wishes to protect his realm and constantly enjoy happiness; who wishes to cause all sentient beings to receive peace and security; who wishes to subdue all external enemies and ensure that his own kingdom flourishes forever; and who wishes to cause the True Teaching to spread throughout the world so that suffering and evil dharmas are all extinguished.
"Blessed One!
These rulers of nations will surely listen to and receive this wondrous King of Sutras; they should also respectfully make offerings to, read, recite, and uphold those who do so.

By the power of these roots of goodness from hearing the Dharma, we and the other immeasurable hosts of devas shall partake of the flavor of the unsurpassed nectar of the Dharma, increase all our retinues, and ensure that all other celestial beings likewise attain supreme benefit."
Why is this? Because this king of men listens to and receives this sutra with a sincere heart.
World-Honored One!

Just as Mahābrahmā constantly proclaims both mundane and supramundane treatises for all sentient beings, Śakra further expounds various treatises, and the seers possessing the five supernatural powers also discourse upon various treatises.
“World-Honored One!

Although Brahmā, Śakra, and the seers with the five supernormal powers possess hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of immeasurable treatises, yet because the Buddha, the World-Honored One, out of compassion and pity, has preached the subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* for the sake of the multitudes of devas and humans, it surpasses all those previously mentioned by hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of times, beyond any possible comparison.”

Why is this? Because by means of this, all the kings of Jambudvīpa may transform the world with the True Dharma (*saddharma*), bringing about matters that grant peace and happiness to sentient beings; they shall protect themselves and their retinues so that they are free from suffering and affliction, and shall not be harmed by enemies or bandits from other regions; all evils shall depart far away, and calamities within the realm shall be dispelled, as they transform the people through the True Dharma such that there is no litigation or strife.

Therefore, O World-Honored One, each king among men should, within his own realm, uphold the torch of the Dharma so that it shines brightly and boundlessly, increasing the merit of the celestial hosts and their retinues.
World-Honored One!

We, the four kings, together with the immeasurable hosts of devas and yakṣas, and all the devas within Jambudvīpa, by this cause and condition shall partake of the flavor of the unsurpassed nectar of the Dharma; we shall obtain great majesty, power, and radiance, being fully endowed with them; all sentient beings shall attain peace and security; furthermore, in future ages, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of inconceivable nayuta kalpas, they shall constantly experience happiness; they shall further encounter immeasurable Buddhas, plant various roots of goodness, and thereafter realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Such immeasurable and boundless benefits are all due to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, who, through his great compassion, surpasses the hosts of Brahmās; through his great wisdom, exceeds Śakra; and through his cultivation of various ascetic practices, excels the rishis of the five supernatural powers by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas—beyond calculation. For the sake of all sentient beings, he has expounded such a subtle and wondrous sūtra, enabling all the sovereigns of Jambudvīpa and the multitudes of people to clearly understand all worldly laws, the governance of states, the transformation of men, and matters of exhortation. By the power of the circulation of this King of Sūtras, all shall universally attain peace and happiness.
These benefits and merits are all due to the power of the Great Teacher Śākyamuni’s compassion in widely disseminating this sutra.
World-Honored One!
For these reasons, all kings and rulers of men should uphold, make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise this wondrous King of Sutras.
Why is this? Because such inconceivable and supreme merits benefit all beings; therefore, it is called the Supreme King of Sutras.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Four Heavenly Kings:

"You Four Kings, along with your retinues and the immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of devas, should protect and guard that king of men who, with a sincere heart, hears this sutra, makes offerings to it, reveres it, respects it, and praises it; you shall eliminate his misfortunes and afflictions, enabling him to bring peace and happiness to you as well.

If the fourfold assembly can widely disseminate this king of sutras, they will extensively perform the Buddha’s work among humans and devas, universally benefiting immeasurable sentient beings. Such persons, you Four Kings, must always protect and guard."

Thus, you fourfold assembly, do not allow yourselves to be disturbed by external conditions; rather, let your bodies and minds be tranquil and at ease, so that this King of Sutras may be widely proclaimed and disseminated without interruption, benefiting sentient beings until the end of the future.
At that time, the Heavenly King Vaśavartin rose from his seat and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I possess a dhāraṇī method of the wish-fulfilling jewel. If there are sentient beings who delight in receiving and upholding it, their merit shall be immeasurable.”
I shall constantly provide protection so that those sentient beings may be freed from suffering and attain happiness, and be able to accomplish the two kinds of provisions: merit and wisdom.
Those who wish to uphold [this teaching] should first recite this mantra for protecting the body.
He then spoke the mantra:

"Namo vairocanāya mahārājāya | Tadyathā | ra ra ra ra | kuṇu kuṇu | kūṇu kūṇu | kṣuṇu kṣuṇu | sva sva karaka | kara mahāvikarman | mahāvikarman | mahārāja | hūṃ kṣa hūṃ kṣa | [Name of oneself] tuṃ | Sarvasattvānām ca svāhā. "World-Honored One! [he said.]
One who recites this mantra should consecrate a white thread with it seven times, tying a knot at each repetition, and fasten it behind the elbow; thus the task will surely be accomplished.

One should take various incenses—namely, agallochum, sandalwood, camphor, storax, tagara, and frankincense—and mix them in equal parts. Holding an incense burner, one should burn the incense as an offering, bathe until pure, and wear fresh, clean garments. In a quiet chamber, one may then recite the divine mantra to invoke me, the Deva Vaiśravaṇa.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:

“Namo vaiśramaṇāya | Namo dānadāya | Dāniścarāya | Aghaṭe | Apadamiṭa | Dāniścara | Pramā | Kāruṇika | Sarvasattva | Hita-kṣema | Mama [insert name here] dānamanu-praracaya | Svayaṃ-maghaṭe | Svāhā. Having recited this mantra seven times, one should then recite the root mantra.
When wishing to recite the mantra, one should first invoke the names and pay homage to the Triple Gem, as well as to the Celestial King Vaiśravaṇa.
He is able to bestow wealth and property, causing the aspirations of all sentient beings to be fulfilled; he can accomplish everything and grant them peace and happiness.

Having paid homage in this manner, one next recites the Heart Mantra of the Wish-Fulfilling Maṇi Jewel of the Celestial King Vaiśravaṇa, which can bestow upon sentient beings peace and happiness according to their wishes.
At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, before the Buddha, spoke this heart-mantra of the wish-fulfilling maṇi jewel:
"Namo ratnatrayāya | namo vaiśravaṇāya mahārājāya ||"
Tadyathā: cimi cimi sumu sumu.

*Manorathaprapūraka-ye svāhā.* When receiving and upholding this mantra, first recite it one thousand times. Thereafter, within a clean room, smear the ground with *gomaya* (cow dung) to create a small altar. At all times, provide food and drink, make offerings with single-minded devotion, and constantly burn exquisite incense so that the smoke does not cease.
Reciting the aforementioned heart-mantra, he focused his mind day and night, listening only with his own ears and not allowing others to understand it.
At that time, a prince of the Vaiśravaṇas named Caṇḍīśa appeared in the form of a youth and came to his location.
He asked,
"For what reason must you summon my father?
and one may then reply:
"I wish to make offerings to the Triple Gem and require wealth for this purpose; I pray that you will grant it to me.
When the artisan heard these words, he immediately returned to his father's place and said to him:
"There is now a virtuous person who has given rise to a heart of utmost sincerity to make offerings to the Triple Gem, yet they lack sufficient wealth; it is for this reason they have sent for us."
His father replied, "You may go quickly;

give him one hundred *kāriṣapaṇas* every day. This is the original Sanskrit term; however, depending on the region, it refers either to cowrie shells or to coins made of gold, silver, copper, iron, and so forth. Currently in Magadha, one *kāriṣapaṇa* generally consists of one thousand six hundred cowrie shells, though the total number can be inferred based on the value of the goods, as the amount varies by location.
If a person who maintains the mantra attains accomplishment, they will know the quantity of the objects obtained at the time of their acquisition.
According to one version of the text:
"Every day, one hundred *cennaras* [are given], which is to say, gold coins."
"Furthermore, one shall obtain [the results] daily for as long as one lives. Those who seek [this] in the West often experience divine efficacy, except in cases where they lack a sincere heart.
Once the mantra-holder has seen these signs, they will know that the rite has been accomplished.
One should dwell alone in a clean room, burn incense, and lie down to sleep.
One may place a casket of incense by the side of the bed; every time at dawn, one should look into the casket to obtain the desired object.

Whenever one obtains goods, they must be offered to the Triple Gem on that very day; incense, flowers, food, and drink should also be bestowed upon the poor and destitute until all are exhausted, and nothing should be kept back.
Give rise to thoughts of loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings; do not harbor thoughts of anger, deceit, flattery, or malice.
If anger arises, the spiritual efficacy will be lost; you must constantly guard your mind and ensure that no resentment or hatred occurs.

Furthermore, those who uphold this mantra should, throughout each day, call to mind me, the Heavenly King Bahudhātī, along with my male and female retinues, praising and extolling them. By constantly supporting one another through the ten wholesome paths of action, they shall cause the power of merit of those devas to increase and brighten, so that all manner of virtues may universally reach them as they realize the state of Bodhi.
When those hosts of devas witness this event, they all rejoice greatly and come together to protect and guard the mantra-holder.

Furthermore, the life span of the mantra-holder shall be long and far-reaching; for immeasurable years, he will forever be free from the three miserable realms and constantly devoid of calamities. He shall also obtain wish-fulfilling jewels and hidden treasures, possessing sovereign supernatural powers so that all his aspirations are fulfilled.
If one seeks official rank and glory, there shall be nothing that does not accord with one's wishes; one will also understand the speech of all birds and beasts.
"World-Honored One!

If, while upholding this mantra, one desires to see my own form appear, one may do so on the eighth or fifteenth day of the month by painting an image of the Buddha upon white cotton cloth, using wood-glue and various colors for its adornment; the person who paints this image must observe the Eight Precepts."
To the left of the Buddha, one should depict the goddess Śrī; to the right of the Buddha, one should depict myself, the god Mañjuśrī, along with their male and female attendants.

Arrange the seats so that all are in accordance with the Dharma; array flowers and colored ornaments, burn various famous incenses, and light lamps to maintain constant illumination without ceasing day or night. With the most excellent food and drink and all manner of rare delicacies, make offerings at the appropriate times with a heart of profound sincerity, upholding the divine mantra without a frivolous mind.
When summoning me, you should recite this mantra: "Namo śrījināya buddhāya."
Homage to the yakṣa king Vaiśravaṇa,
the great king, the lord of the earth.
Namo śrīye mahādevīye tadyathā.
tara tara tura tura mara mara

Vajra-vaiḍūrya-muktikā-kaṅkṛta-śrī-rājñi.
Pūrvam sarvasattvahitakāma vaiśravaṇa śrīyatibhibhadra svāhā.
Mihī mihī ma-vilambā gūḷha gūḷha ṛṣabha ṛṣabha dharma dharma buddha he mama.

*Svāhā*. “World-Honored One!
If I see this person reciting the mantra, and further see such abundant offerings being made, I shall immediately give rise to a heart of loving-kindness, affection, and joy.”

I shall immediately transform my body into the form of a child, or take the appearance of an old man or a bhikṣu, holding in my hand a wish-fulfilling maṇi jewel as well as a golden pouch, and enter the maṇḍala. Manifesting reverence with my body and reciting the Buddha’s name with my mouth, I shall say to the mantra-holder:
"Whatever you seek, I shall cause it all to be fulfilled according to your wishes."

"Whether they hide in forests and thickets, or fashion precious gems, or desire to be beloved by the multitude, or seek gold, silver, and other such things, they wish to employ various mantras so that all may be efficacious."
Whether one desires supernormal powers, a long life, or sublime bliss, there is nothing that will not accord with one's heart's desire.
I have now spoken of such matters; if you seek anything further, all shall be accomplished according to your wishes, with inexhaustible treasuries of jewels and boundless merit.

Even if the sun and moon were to fall to the earth, or even if the great earth were ever to shift its position, this truthful word of mine shall never be in vain; may I always attain peace and security, and experience joy according to my heart's desire.
World-Honored One!
If there are those who can receive, uphold, read, and recite this king of sutras, when they chant this mantra, they will do so without fatigue, and the Dharma will be swiftly accomplished.
World-Honored One!

For the sake of those sentient beings who are impoverished, distressed, and afflicted by suffering, I shall now recite this divine mantra to cause them to obtain great benefit, so that they may all attain wealth and joy, sovereignty and freedom from affliction. Until the end of their lives, I shall protect them, following after these people to eliminate their calamities and misfortunes.

Furthermore, I shall cause those who propagate this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, as well as those who maintain its mantras, to be illuminated by my radiance within a distance of a hundred paces; I, along with my thousand yakṣa deities, will also constantly attend and protect them, serving their every desire so that nothing remains unfulfilled.
"I speak words of truth, free from falsehood; may the Buddha alone bear witness to this.
When the Heavenly King Bahudhātī had finished reciting this mantra, the Buddha said:
"Excellent!"
"O Heavenly King!

You are able to tear asunder the net of poverty and suffering of all sentient beings and cause them to attain wealth and joy; by reciting this divine mantra, you further cause this sutra to circulate widely throughout the world."

Then the Four Great Kings all rose from their seats, bared one shoulder, prostrated at his feet, knelt with their right knees on the ground, and with palms joined in reverence, praised the Buddha’s virtues with these sublime verses:
“The Buddha’s face is like the pure, full moon, And like a thousand suns emitting radiance;
His eyes are pure, long, and wide like blue lotuses, His teeth are white, even, and closely set like jade or snow.”
The Buddha’s virtues are boundless like the great ocean, With infinite wondrous jewels accumulated within;
The waters of wisdom and virtue are ever full, Completely filled with hundreds of thousands of supreme concentrations.
The marks of wheels upon your feet are all exquisitely adorned; the hub, rim, and thousand spokes are perfectly even.
Your hands and feet are fully embellished with webbed membranes, complete with all the characteristics of a king of swans.
The radiance of the Buddha’s body is like a mountain of gold, pure, extraordinary, and without peer;
it is also like Mount Sumeru, replete with merit. Therefore, I bow my head to the King of Buddhas.
The marks and signs are like space, unfathomable; they surpass a thousand moons in radiating light.
All are like flames or illusions, inconceivable; therefore, I bow my head with a mind free from attachment.
At that time, after the Four Heavenly Kings had praised the Buddha, the World-Honored One also replied to them in verse:
"This most supreme *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, Spoken by the Unsurpassed One of Ten Powers;
You, the Four Kings, shall always provide protection, And should give rise to a courageous and non-regressive mind."
This wondrous jewel of a sutra is exceedingly profound, Able to bestow happiness upon all sentient beings;
Because those beings dwell in peace and joy, It shall always circulate throughout Jambudvīpa.
Within this great trichiliocosm, may all classes of sentient beings—
those in the realms of hungry ghosts, animals, and hells— be entirely freed from such miserable destinies.
The kings who dwell in this southern continent, And all other classes of sentient beings;
By the power of this sutra, they shall always rejoice, Receiving protection and attaining peace and security.
May all sentient beings within this land likewise be freed from the suffering of various illnesses and from thieves and robbers;
because this kingdom propagates the sutras, may it be peaceful, secure, abundant, and joyful, free from conflict and affliction.
If a person hears and receives this king of sutras, desiring nobility and wealth and profit;
may their land be abundant, peaceful, and free from strife, and may all their heart’s wishes be fulfilled accordingly.
It can cause the enemies of other lands to retreat and scatter, ensuring perpetual peace and security within one's own realm;
through the power of this most supreme King of Sutras, one is freed from all suffering and affliction, remaining without grief or fear.
Just as a king of jewel trees within a palace can produce all manner of articles of pleasure,
so too is this most supreme King of Sutras able to bestow upon the King of Men excellent merits.
Just as clear, pure, and cool water can eliminate hunger, thirst, and all fevers of affliction;
so too is this most excellent King of Sutras, which brings fulfillment to the hearts of those who delight in merit.
Just as a person may have a precious casket in their chamber, from which all that they require for use comes according to their heart’s desire;
so too it is with this most excellent King of Sutras—merit follows the mind, lacking nothing.
You, O Lord of Devas and your celestial hosts, should make offerings to this King of Sutras;
if you can uphold this sutra according to its teachings, you will be fully endowed with wisdom and majestic spiritual power.
All Buddhas of the ten directions in the present Together protect and keep this King of Sutras in mind;
Seeing those who read, recite, and uphold it, They praise them, saying, "Excellent! How truly rare!"
If there be anyone who can hear this sutra, their body and mind will leap for joy and give rise to gladness;
at all times, hundreds of thousands of yakṣas will follow wherever they dwell to protect such a person.
The hosts of devas in this world, In number immeasurable and inconceivable,
All together listen to and receive this King of Sutras, Rejoicing in its protection and upholding, never regressing.
If a person hears and receives this King of Sutras, their majestic power and valor will be ever sovereign;
they shall increase the hosts of all humans and devas, causing them to leave behind decay and affliction and to gain increased radiance.
At that time, having heard these verses, the Four Heavenly Kings were filled with joy and leaped for gladness, and they addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
From the past until now, we have never before heard such a profound and subtle Dharma.”

His heart was filled with both sorrow and joy; tears flowed from his eyes as they mingled together, and his entire body trembled as he realized this inconceivable and rare event. He then scattered heavenly *māndārava* flowers and *mahāmāndārava* flowers over the Buddha.
Having made this sublime offering to the Buddha, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
We four kings each have five hundred yakṣa retinues who shall constantly protect this sutra and the Dharma-preacher in every place, providing assistance and defense through the light of wisdom."

Regarding any points of meaning in this sutra that may be forgotten, I shall cause them all to be remembered without loss, and I shall grant them the sublime Dharma-gate of dhāraṇī so that they may attain it in its entirety.

Furthermore, he wished that this most supreme King of Sūtras, wherever it might be, would be widely proclaimed and disseminated for the sake of all sentient beings, so that it would not quickly disappear.

At that time, while the World-Honored One was preaching this Dharma within the great assembly, immeasurable sentient beings all attained great wisdom, sagacity, and eloquence; they gathered an immeasurable accumulation of merit, were freed from all sorrow and affliction, gave rise to a heart of joy and bliss, became skillfully clear regarding all treatises, ascended the path of transcendence, never again regressed, and swiftly realized Bodhi.

Chapter Thirteen: The Dhāraṇī of Non-Attachment (7) At that time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Śāriputra:

"There is now a Dharma gate called the *Asaṅga-dhāraṇī* (Dhāraṇī of Non-Attachment). It is the practice cultivated by all Bodhisattvas; it was upheld by the Bodhisattvas of the past, and it is the mother of Bodhisattvas."
When he had spoken these words, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the meaning of the term ‘dhāraṇī’?”
“World-Honored One!
A dhāraṇī is neither a location nor a non-location.
Having spoken these words, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra:
“Excellent! Excellent, Śāriputra!”
You have already been able to give rise to faith and understanding regarding the Mahāyāna, and you hold the Mahāyāna in high esteem.

As you have said, this dhāraṇī is not a location, nor is it a non-location; it is not a dharma, nor is it a non-dharma; it is not of the past, the future, or the present; it is not a thing, nor is it a non-thing; it is not a condition, nor is it a non-condition; it is not activity, nor is it a non-activity; therein no dharma arises, nor does any dharma cease.
Nevertheless, for the sake of benefiting all bodhisattvas, I have spoken thus.

This establishment of the power, the correct principles, and the essential approach of this dhāraṇī’s efficacy is itself the merit of all buddhas, the prohibitions and precepts of all buddhas, that which all buddhas study, the secret intent of all buddhas, and the birthplace of all buddhas; therefore, it is called the most sublime dharma-gate of the *Anupalipta-dhāraṇī* (The Untainted Dhāraṇī).
Having spoken these words, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I pray that the Sugata will explain this dharma of dhāraṇī for me.”

If bodhisattvas are able to abide in this, they will no longer regress from unsurpassed enlightenment; they will fulfill their right vows, attain non-reliance, and achieve intrinsic eloquence; they will obtain rare and marvelous qualities and dwell securely in the noble path—all because they have attained this dhāraṇī.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said.
If there is a bodhisattva who attains this dhāraṇī, one should know that such a person is no different from a Buddha.
If anyone makes offerings to, honors, serves, or provides for this bodhisattva, one should know that they are making offerings to the Buddha.

Śāriputra! If there are others who hear this dhāraṇī, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, and give rise to faith and understanding, they too should be honored and provided for with offerings just as one would for the Buddha, without distinction; by such causes and conditions, they shall attain the unsurpassed fruit.
At that time, the World-Honored One then expounded the dhāraṇī, saying:

“Tadyathā | sandharani | uddharani | susamparistite | sunama | suparistite viśaye | vara | sadye | pratisnye | su-āroha | snyana-mate | upatani | avanamate | abhisatani | abhivyehara | śubha | vati | suniśrita bha-guñja abhibuddha svāhā. The Buddha addressed Śāriputra:

"If there is a bodhisattva who can skillfully abide in and correctly uphold these dhāraṇī phrases free from defilement and attachment, it should be known that this person’s rightly made vows will never be exhausted—whether for one kalpa, a hundred kalpas, a thousand kalpas, or a hundred thousand kalpas—and their body shall not be harmed by swords or staves, poisons, water or fire, or fierce beasts."
Why is this? Śāriputra,
this *Dhāraṇī* of Non-Attachment is the mother of all Buddhas of the past, the mother of all Buddhas of the future, and the mother of all Buddhas of the present.

Śāriputra! If there were someone who, for the sake of all Buddhas, offered as a gift seven precious jewels filling ten *asaṃkhyeya* trichiliocosms, along with supreme and exquisite clothing, food, drink, and various other offerings, continuing for countless eons;

Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because this profound Dharma gate of the *Anupalipta-dhāraṇī* is the mother of all Buddhas.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra and the great assembly, having heard this Dharma, were all filled with great joy and vowed to receive and uphold it.

Chapter 14: The Chapter on the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel (7) The Sutra of the Golden Light, Supreme King, Chapter Fourteen: The Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Then, in the midst of the great assembly, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:

“You should know that there is a dhāraṇī named ‘Wish-Fulfilling Jewel,’ which distances one from all calamities and misfortunes and can also ward off all evil thunderbolts; it was proclaimed by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past.”

At this time, within this sutra, I likewise proclaim it for you, the great assembly; it shall bring great benefit to humans and devas, have compassion for the world, protect all beings, and cause them to attain peace and happiness.
At that time, the great assembly and Ānanda, having heard the Buddha’s words, each with utmost sincerity gazed up at the World-Honored One and listened to receive the divine mantra.
The Buddha said:
"Listen attentively! In this eastern direction, there is a King of Lightning named Agada."
In the south there is the Lightning King of Radiance named Śatru;
in the west there is the Lightning King of Radiance named Bahuprabha;
in the north there is the Lightning King of Radiance named Sūtamani.

If any son or daughter of good family hears the names of these kings of lightning and knows their respective locations, that person shall immediately be far removed from all matters of fear, and all calamities and misfortunes shall be entirely extinguished.

If one writes down the names of these four directional kings of lightning within one's dwelling, there will be no fear of thunder and lightning in that place; furthermore, calamities, misfortunes, and all obstructive afflictions, as well as untimely and unjust deaths, shall all be completely removed.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:

“Tadyathā | nime nime nime | nimindare | sthiraloke | lokajini | sthiraśūlabhāṇi | hulu hulu | hulu hulu | May I, [Name], and this dwelling place be entirely freed from all terrors, all sufferings, lightning, thunderbolts, and even untimely death; svāhā.”

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, being amidst the great assembly, rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

I shall now, before the Buddha, briefly proclaim this divine mantra of the wish-fulfilling jewel, which brings great benefit to all humans and devas; out of compassion for the world, it protects all beings, causing them to attain peace and happiness, possessing great majestic power so that all their aspirations are fulfilled as they wish.
He then spoke the mantra,
saying: "Tadyathā hṛte."
Vihate nivate pratisṭhite jaye.
Pratimittire śuddhimukte vimale.
Praprasūre antare panthare svasti pantharāpasiṇi.
Hre-keta-re kapi-le piṅgala-ocike.
Dadati mukhi kṣa kṣa.

"May I, [Name], and this dwelling place be entirely freed from all terrors and all suffering, even unto untimely death. May I never behold evil things, but always be protected and sustained by the majestic light of the Great Compassion of the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. Svāhā."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, rose from his seat, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

I shall now also proclaim a dhāraṇī mantra called "Unconquerable," which brings great benefit to all humans and devas, out of compassion for the world, protects all beings, possesses great majestic power, and fulfills all that is sought according to one's wishes.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:
"Tadyathā | muñce muñce | muṇḍe | matī matī | sumatī | mahāmatī | hā hā hā | mabha | ina siddhe | pāpa | vajrapāṇi | oṃ jvalita svāhā. "World-Honored One! [he continued].

This divine mantra of mine is called "Invincible Protection. If any man or woman single-mindedly receives and maintains it, writes it down, recites it, and remembers it without forgetting, I shall constantly protect that person day and night, causing them to be entirely free from all terrors, even up to unjust death.
At that time, Brahmā Śikhin, the Lord of the Sahā World, rose from his seat, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

I also possess a subtle Dharma gate of dhāraṇī, which brings great benefit to all humans and devas; out of compassion for the world, it protects all beings, possesses great majestic power, and fulfills whatever is sought according to one's wishes.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:
"Tadyathā | hiri | miri | dirī | svāhā | varadāmbhoruhe | varadamamani | varadamakevi | puṣpasaṃstare | svāhā. "World-Honored One! [he said.]

This divine mantra of mine is named "Brahma-Cure"; it is fully capable of protecting those who uphold this mantra, causing them to be free from sorrow, affliction, and all sinful karma, and ensuring they remain entirely distant from even untimely death.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, rose from his seat, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!

I also possess a dhāraṇī named Vajraśānti. It is a great vidyā-mantra capable of removing all terrors, calamities, and misfortunes, even including untimely death; it causes one to be entirely free from these, uproots suffering, bestows happiness, and benefits both humans and devas."
He then spoke the mantra:

“Tadyathā | Vinī | Varṇī | Paṇḍamaḍanadhimarṇiṭi | Ilguri | Gandhari | Caṇḍali | Mātangi | Pukkasī | Śabarī | Bhille | Ḍāmini | Mahurāṇī | Darāṇī | Kicakravāci | Śavari | Śavari | Svāhā. At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka, and the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa all rose from their seats, joined their palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

I also now possess a divine mantra named "Bestowing Fearlessness upon All Sentient Beings," which constantly provides protection against all suffering and affliction, enabling them to attain peace and happiness, increase their lifespan, and remain free from all ailments and pain, even distancing themselves entirely from untimely death.
He then spoke the mantra:

“Tadyathā | puṣpe | supuṣpe | dumaparihaṇe | āryaparāśasite | śāntinirmukte | maṅgale sudṛṣṭe | siddhibhūte | svāhā. At that time, there were also various great nāga kings—namely, the nāga king Manasvin, the nāga king Vidyutprabha, the nāga king Anavatapta, the nāga king Vidyujjihva, and the nāga king Suprabha—who all rose from their seats, joined their palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

I also possess a *dhāraṇī* of the wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*), which can ward off evil lightning, eliminate all terrors, and bring great benefit to humans and devas. Out of compassion for the world, it protects all beings; it possesses great majestic power, fulfills all wishes as they are made, and causes even untimely deaths to be entirely avoided. It causes all poisons to cease and brings to total extinction all malevolent practices involving sorcery, incantations, and inauspicious rites.

I now offer this divine mantra to the World-Honored One; I only pray that you will compassionately accept it out of your loving-kindness and pity, and thereby cause us to leave this dragon realm forever and abandon our stinginess and greed.
Why is this? Because it is due to this stinginess and greed that one undergoes various sufferings within the cycle of birth and death; we vow to sever the seeds of stinginess and greed.
Then they spoke this mantra:
*Tadyathā | ajale | amale | amṛte | akṣaye | abhaye | puṇyaparīyāṣṭe | sarvabuddhapratyaṃśmaniye | svāhā | arīye bandhu | supuṇyaye svāhā.* "World-Honored One!"

If there are good sons or good daughters who speak this dhāraṇī mantra from their mouths, or who write it in a scroll, receive, uphold, read, recite, respect, and make offerings to it, they will ultimately be forever free from thunder, lightning, and thunderbolts, as well as all terrors, afflictions, and misfortunes, even unto untimely death;
furthermore, no poisons, sorcery, malevolent spells, or curses, nor harmful beasts such as tigers, wolves, lions, and venomous snakes, down to mosquitoes and gadflies, shall cause them any harm.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly:
"Excellent! Excellent!"

These divine mantras all possess great power; they can fulfill whatever matters sentient beings seek according to their hearts' desires, providing great benefit, provided that one does not lack sincerity.
You should have no doubts about this.
When the great assembly had heard the Buddha’s words, they rejoiced, believed, and accepted them.

On the eighth day of the waxing moon, when the moon is in conjunction with the Puṣya asterism, one may recite this mantra for invocation:
“Tadyathā: ciri ciri, curu curu, kuru kuru, kuṭu kuṭu, tuṭu tuṭu, svāhā, svāhā, vaśa vaśa, svāhā. “World-Honored One!”
Regarding this divine mantra, if there are members of the fourfold assembly who recite it one hundred and eight times to summon me, I shall immediately come to their invocation for their sake.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!
If there are sentient beings who wish to see my manifested body and converse with me, they should likewise arrange the ritual procedures as previously described and recite this divine mantra:
“Tadyathā | Añjani | Kṣaṇi | Śini | Dahari | Ha ha hi hi kuru | Vare | Svāhā. World-Honored One!

If a person maintains this mantra, they should recite it one hundred and eight times, together with the preceding mantra; I shall certainly manifest my form and fulfill all their wishes, ensuring that nothing remains unaccomplished. It shall never be in vain.
If one wishes to recite this mantra, one should first recite the mantra for protecting the body, which says:
"Tadyathā | niśrīmaśa keṭi | naṭi kuṭi | bṛdhi bṛdhe | bṛṭi bṛṭi | ku-kuṭi | kha-pa-ci-li | svāhā. "World-Honored One!"

When reciting this mantra, take a five-colored thread, recite the mantra twenty-one times, and tie twenty-one knots. Fasten it behind the elbow of the left arm; one will then be protected from harm and have nothing to fear.

If there be anyone who recites this mantra with a sincere heart, their aspirations shall surely be fulfilled. I do not speak falsely; I take the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha as my solemn pledge to certify that this is true.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Earth Goddess, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
Since you are able to protect this King of Sutras and the preacher of the Dharma with this mantra of truthful speech, by these causes and conditions, you shall obtain immeasurable rewards of merit.

Chapter 19: The Great Yakṣa General Senāpati (8) The Sūtra of the Golden Light, Supreme King, Chapter Nineteen: The Great Yakṣa General Senāpati At that time, the great yakṣa general Senāpati, together with the yakṣa deities of the twenty-eight divisions, rose from their seats within the great assembly. They bared their right shoulders, placed their right knees upon the ground, and with palms joined toward the Buddha, addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!

World-Honored One! Wherever this *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-uttamarāja-sūtra* is proclaimed and circulated—whether in cities or villages, mountain marshes or empty forests, in royal palaces or monastic dwellings—in the present world and in future worlds; World-Honored One! [there it shall be so.]

I, the yakṣa general Saṃśītirya, together with the yakṣa deities of the twenty-eight divisions, shall go to that place; each concealing our forms, we shall protect that Dharma-preacher wherever he may be, causing him to be free from decline and affliction, and always to enjoy peace and happiness.

Furthermore, whether they be men or women, boys or girls, those who hear this Dharma and even receive and uphold a single four-line verse from this sutra, or hold a single phrase, or recite with devotion and make offerings to the title of this King of Sutras at its beginning, or to the name of a single Tathāgata or a single Bodhisattva found within this sutra—having resolved their minds to do so—I shall protect, guard, and embrace them, ensuring they are free from calamities and misfortunes, and that they leave suffering behind to attain happiness.
"Bhagavān!
For what reason am I named 'Rightly Comprehending' (Samyakprajñā)?

This is the causal basis: it is that which the Buddha has personally realized; I know all dharmas, I understand all dharmas, according to all dharmas as they exist, and according to the distinctions in the categories and essential natures of all dharmas, Bhagavān!"
"Regarding these dharmas, I am able to fully comprehend them.

I possess the light of inconceivable wisdom; I possess the torch of inconceivable wisdom; I possess the practice of inconceivable wisdom; I possess the accumulation of inconceivable wisdom; and I am able to penetrate the realm of inconceivable wisdom."
"Bhagavān!
Just as I have right knowledge, right understanding, and right awakening regarding all phenomena, so am I able to observe them correctly.
Bhagavān!"
For these reasons, I, the yakṣa general, am named "Rightly Understanding.

By virtue of this principle, I can cause that teacher who expounds the Dharma to have speech and eloquence that are clear and fully adorned; I can also cause vital energy to enter through his pores, so that his physical strength becomes sufficient, his majestic spirit and valor are robust, and he achieves inconceivable light of wisdom. He shall attain right mindfulness without any retreat or discouragement; his body shall be strengthened and never decline, his faculties shall be at ease and joyful, and he shall constantly experience delight.

For this reason, for the sake of those sentient beings who have already planted roots of goodness and cultivated meritorious deeds under hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, [this teaching] shall be widely proclaimed and disseminated throughout Jambudvīpa, so that it does not quickly disappear.

When those sentient beings have heard this sutra, they will attain the light of inconceivable great wisdom and an immeasurable accumulation of merit and knowledge. In future lives, they shall experience the supreme joys of humans and devas for an incalculable number of *koṭi-nayuta* kalpas; they shall constantly encounter all Buddhas and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, never again passing through the three miserable realms or the realm of Yama, which are characterized by extreme suffering.
At that time, the yakṣa general Samantabhadra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I possess a dhāraṇī which I shall now personally declare before the Buddha, out of a desire to benefit and have compassion for all sentient beings.”
He then spoke the mantra, saying:
"Namo buddhāya, namo dharmāya."
Namo saṃghāya | Namo varuṇāya | Namo indrāya ||
Namo chetunam mo harajanam tadyatha.

"Furthermore, if there be anyone who is able to receive and uphold this vidyā-mantra, I shall provide them with the necessities of life and articles of comfort—food, drink, clothing, flowers, fruits, and rare treasures; or if they seek sons, daughters, boys, girls, gold, silver, precious gems, or various necklaces and ornaments—I shall supply all these according to their wishes and requests, ensuring that they lack for nothing."
This vidyā-mantra possesses great power; when it is recited, I shall swiftly arrive at that place, ensuring there are no obstacles and that all is accomplished according to one's wishes.

When reciting this mantra, one should know the following ritual: first, draw an image of the yakṣa Saṃjñeya, four or five feet in height, holding a spear and a trident. Before this image, construct a square altar and place four full jars of honey-water or sugar-water, along with unguents, powdered incense, burning incense, and various flower garlands.

Furthermore, one should construct an earthen fire-pit before the mandala; place charcoal embers within it and burn *soma* and mustard seeds in the pit while reciting the aforementioned mantra one hundred and eight times, burning one seed with each recitation.
Even unto the point where I, the yakṣa general, manifest my own form and ask the practitioner of mantras:
"What do you require?
What is it that you seek in your heart?"
I immediately answered him according to the facts, and I then fulfilled all his requests exactly as he had spoken.

Whether he required gold, silver, or various hidden treasures; whether he desired to become a divine seer (*ṛṣi*) traveling through the air; whether he sought the supernormal power of the divine eye (*divyacakṣus-abhijñā*), or the knowledge of others' thoughts—regarding all sentient beings, I granted him mastery according to his wishes, causing him to sever the afflictions (*kleśa*) and swiftly attain liberation, such that everything was accomplished.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the yakṣa general Suvijñāpta, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"You are able to thus benefit all sentient beings by proclaiming this divine mantra; you protect the True Dharma, and your merit and benefit shall be boundless. Chapter 20:

The Righteous Discourse on Royal Law (8) The Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra, Chapter Twenty: The Righteous Discourse on Royal Law. At that time, the Earth Goddess named Dṛḍhā rose from her seat amidst the great assembly, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, joined her palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."

Among all nations, those who act as kings for the people—if they lack the True Dharma—will be unable to govern the country, provide for and nourish sentient beings, or maintain their own persons in the exalted position for long;

I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion and pity, will expound for me the essential treatise on the Righteous Dharma of Kingship and the essentials of statecraft, so that when these human kings have heard the Dharma, they may practice according to the teaching and transform the world rightly, thereby ensuring that the exalted position remains forever secure and peaceful, and that all the people within the realm receive benefit.
At that time, the World-Honored One, in the midst of the great assembly, addressed the Earth Goddess Dṛḍhā, saying:
"Listen attentively!
In the past there was a king named Baladhvaja. That king had a son named Citradhvaja; not long after he had received the position of consecration, his father, the King, said to Citradhvaja:"

"There is a treatise on the correct principles of royal governance called the *Devendrasamaya*. In the past, when I had received the consecration and served as the sovereign of the realm, my father, the King named Jñānabala-dhvaja, expounded this treatise on the correct principles of royal governance for me."

Relying on this treatise, I have governed the kingdom well for twenty thousand years; I do not recall ever having entertained a single thought of acting contrary to the Dharma. You, too, should act in this manner today; do not govern the kingdom through unrighteous means.
"What is called the Right Discourse on the Dharma of Kings?
Listen well now, and I shall explain it to you.
Thereupon, King Baladharaketu spoke this Right Discourse in sublime verses for his son:
"I have taught this discourse on the Dharma for kings, to bring benefit and peace to all sentient beings;
it is intended to sever the doubts of the world and to eliminate all faults."
All you lords of the devas, And likewise the kings among men,
Should give rise to a heart of joy And listen with palms joined as I speak.
In the past, the hosts of devas Assembled upon the Vajra Mountain;
The Four Kings rose from their seats and questioned the Great Brahmā:
“O Lord of Brahmā, most supreme and honored one; Sovereign of Great Freedom among the gods!
We pray that you will take pity on us and sever all our doubts.”
How is it that, dwelling in the human world, one earns the name "deva"?
Furthermore, by what causes and conditions is one titled a "son of heaven" (devaputra)?
How is it that, being born among humans, one alone attains the status of lord of men?
"How is it that you dwell in the heavens, and furthermore, have become a Heavenly King?
Having thus questioned that Brahmā King regarding the protection of the world,
the Brahmā Lord immediately spoke to him:
"O Protector of the World, you should know that for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, you have asked me about the methods of governing a kingdom; listen well as I explain them.
By the power of past virtuous karma, one is born in heaven and becomes a king."
If he is among human beings, he shall rule as a sovereign of men;
protected by all the devas, he then enters the mother’s womb,
and once within the womb, the devas continue to guard him.
Though born in the human world, he is called a "deva" because of his supreme dignity;
protected by the various devas, he is also named a "son of heaven.
The Lord of the Thirty-three Devas shares his power with the human king.
And all the devas likewise rely on the power of mastery.
They eliminate all that is unrighteous and cause evil karma not to arise;
they teach sentient beings to cultivate goodness so that they may be born in the heavens.
Humans and the hosts of asuras, along with the gandharvas and others;
rākṣasas and caṇḍālas—all provide half their strength.
Their parents provide half their strength, causing them to abandon evil and cultivate goodness.
The devas collectively protect and sustain them, showing them the various rewards of their wholesome deeds.
If they commit various evil karmas, they cause them to experience those results within this very life;
the devas do not protect them, showing them the various retributions for their evils.
When the people of the land commit evil deeds, and the king neglects them without restraint, this does not accord with correct principle;
they should be disciplined and banished according to the Dharma.
If one sees evil and does not prevent it, unrighteousness will flourish.
Consequently, within the kingdom, deceit and fraud increased day by day.
Seeing the people of the land committing evil without being restrained,
the assembly of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven all gave rise to hearts of indignation.
Consequently, state administration is impaired, and flattery and hypocrisy prevail in the world;
they are invaded by hostile enemies, and their lands are destroyed.
Their households and possessions, as well as their accumulated wealth, are all lost.
Various forms of flattery and deception arise, and they further encroach upon and plunder one another.
Having obtained the kingship through the True Dharma, he does not practice that Dharma;
the people of the land are all dispersed and scattered, like an elephant trampling a lotus pond.
Malign winds arise without constancy, and torrential rains fall out of season;
malevolent stars manifest many portents of change, and the sun and moon are eclipsed, losing their light.
The five grains, various flowers, and fruits—all fail to reach fruition.
When a land suffers famine, it is because the king has abandoned the True Dharma.
If a king abandons the True Dharma and transforms people through evil teachings,
the devas in their original palaces will see this and give rise to sorrow and distress.
Those hosts of celestial kings all spoke these words together:
"This king acts contrary to the Dharma, associating with evil factions.
His royal throne shall not remain secure for long; all the devas are filled with resentment."
Because of that harboring of anger, the kingdom shall perish.
Teaching people through unrighteousness will spread throughout the land;
strife and many deceptions will arise, and epidemics will bring forth manifold sufferings.
The Lord of Devas will not protect him, and all other devas will abandon him;
his kingdom shall perish, and the king’s own body will suffer calamity and distress.
His parents and wife and children, as well as his brothers and sisters—
All shall suffer separation from those they love, even unto death and the end of life.
Meteors shall fall in portents of change, and two suns shall rise at once;
enemies and bandits shall come from other lands, and the people of the nation shall meet with calamity and chaos.
The high ministers whom the state honors shall die by violent and unjust means;
the elephants and horses that it cherishes shall likewise all be lost.
Everywhere there will be the clash of arms, and many people will die through unrighteousness.
Malevolent spirits enter the kingdom, and pestilence spreads everywhere.
The highest ministers of the state, as well as the various counselors;
their hearts harbor flattery and sycophancy, and they all practice what is not the Dharma.
Seeing those who practice unrighteousness, one conceives love and respect for them;
yet toward those who practice the Dharma, one inflicts harsh punishment.
Because of loving and respecting the wicked while punishing the virtuous, [one suffers].
The constellations, winds, and rains will all fail to move according to their proper seasons;
three kinds of calamities will arise, and the True Dharma shall vanish.
Sentient beings will lose their radiance and complexion, and the essence of the earth will all sink away.
From honoring the wicked and slighting the virtuous, there arise three further faults:
unseasonable frost and hail fall, and the sufferings of famine and pestilence spread.
The flavor of all grains and fruits is diminished.
Within that land, sentient beings will suffer many diseases.
The various trees in the country, which once produced sweet and delicious fruits, will all decline because of this;
their fruits will become bitter, astringent, and devoid of flavor.
Formerly there were wonderful groves and delightful places for recreation;
suddenly they all withered away, causing grief and distress to those who saw them.
The rice, wheat, and various fruits—their delicious flavors—gradually vanished.
At the time of eating, the mind finds no joy; how then can the great elements grow?
The radiance and complexion of sentient beings diminish, and their vital strength utterly wastes away;
though they consume food in great abundance, it cannot bring them satiety.
Within the boundaries of that land, all classes of sentient beings will have little strength and no heroic power;
they will be incapable of accomplishing their tasks.
The people of the country will suffer many ailments, and various sufferings will oppress their bodies.
Ghosts and specters spread everywhere, and rākṣasas arise wherever they may be;
if a king acts contrary to the Dharma and associates with evil persons,
the three worlds will consequently suffer decline and ruin.
Such boundless calamities arise within the kingdom;
they all stem from seeing wicked people and failing to abandon them or banish them.
It is through the protection of the devas that one obtains the position of king.
Yet they do not protect the realm with the True Dharma.
If a person cultivates wholesome conduct, they shall be reborn in the heavens;
if one commits evil deeds, upon death they will surely fall into the three miserable realms.
If a king sees his subjects committing transgressions and allows them to persist,
the assembly of the Trāyastriṃśa devas will all give rise to a heart of feverish distress.
They will not obey the instructions of the various devas, nor the words of their parents.
This is one who acts contrary to the Dharma; he is neither a king nor a filial son.
If, within his own realm, he sees one practicing what is contrary to the Dharma, he should punish him in accordance with the Dharma and must not abandon him.
Therefore, the hosts of devas all protect and uphold this king;
for he has extinguished all unwholesome dharmas and is able to cultivate roots of goodness.
In this world, the king will surely bring about retribution in the present life.
Due to his wholesome and unwholesome karma, he practiced equanimity and exhorted sentient beings.
To demonstrate the retribution of good and evil, he became a king of men;
all the devas protected him together, and everyone rejoiced in him.
Through benefiting oneself and others, one should govern the kingdom with the True Dharma;
when one encounters those who are sycophantic and deceitful, they should be dealt with according to the law.
Even if it means losing the royal throne or facing the threat of death, one must remain steadfast.
One shall never practice unwholesome dharmas, but shall abandon them upon seeing their faults.
Among all forms of harm, none is more grievous than the loss of one’s kingdom;
since this is always caused by sycophants and flatterers, they must be punished for this reason.
If there are those who are deceitful and treacherous, they shall lose their royal throne;
because of this, the administration of the king is ruined, like an elephant entering a flower garden.
The Lord of Devas is filled with resentment, and the Asuras are likewise.
Since he is a king of men, he does not rule the country according to [mere] human law.
Therefore, he should govern and punish the wicked in accordance with the Dharma;
he should transform sentient beings through goodness and not comply with what is contrary to the Dharma.
One would rather sacrifice body and life than follow an unrighteous friend;
toward kin and non-kin alike, one regards all with equanimity.
If one is a king of the True Dharma, there shall be no partiality within the realm.
The Dharma King possesses a renowned name, heard throughout the three realms.
The hosts of the Heaven of the Thirty-three rejoice and speak these words:
“The Dharma King of Jambudvīpa is indeed our son.”
"Transform sentient beings through goodness, and govern the nation with the True Dharma;
exhort them to practice the True Dharma, and they shall be born in my palace.
Thus spoke the devas, the various sons of gods, and the hosts of asuras.
Because the King transforms the world through the True Dharma, his mind is always filled with joy.
The hosts of devas all rejoice and together protect the lord of men;
the myriad stars move according to their positions, and the sun and moon do not deviate from their courses.
The harmony of the winds always accords with the seasons, and the sweet rain falls in accordance with the times;
the sprouts and fruits all ripen well, and among people there is no hunger or famine.
All the hosts of devas fill their own palaces.
Therefore, you, O King of Men, should sacrifice your own person to propagate the True Dharma.
You ought to revere the Jewel of the Dharma, for by this the multitude shall find peace and happiness;
you should always remain close to the True Dharma, and its merit will naturally adorn you.
His retinue is always joyful, and he is able to remain far removed from all evils;
transforming sentient beings through the Dharma, he constantly causes them to attain peace and security,
leading all those people to practice the ten wholesome deeds.
The entire land is ever prosperous and joyful, and the kingdom attains peace and security.
The King transforms people through the Dharma, skillfully subduing evil conduct;
he constantly gains a good reputation and brings peace and happiness to all sentient beings.

At that time, all the human kings of the great earth and the vast assembly, having heard the Buddha speak these essential methods for governing a kingdom by the ancient human kings of old, attained what they had never experienced before; they were all greatly rejoiced, and with faith and acceptance, they put them into practice.

21. Chapter on King Sujāta (9). Chapter Twenty-one: On King Sujāta.
At that time, after the Blessed One had expounded the *Rājadharma-samyak-śāstra* for the great assembly, he further addressed the assembly:
"You should listen!
"I shall now explain for you the causes and conditions of my past practice of honoring the Dharma.
At that very moment, he spoke these verses:
"In the past, I was once a Wheel-Turning King; I renounced this great earth along with its vast oceans."
The four continents were filled with rare treasures, which I offered to all the Tathāgatas.
Throughout immeasurable kalpas in the past, seeking the pure and true Dharmakāya,
I relinquished everything I cherished, even my own body and life, without a single thought of stinginess.
Furthermore, in an inconceivable eon of the past, there was a Tathāgata named Ratnaśikhin, the Truly All-Knowing One;
after that Tathāgata had entered parinirvāṇa, a king appeared in the world named Sujāta.
As a Wheel-Turning King, he transformed the four continents; all within the limits of the great ocean submitted to his rule.
There was a city named *Svararuta*, where that Wheel-Turning King resided at that time.
In a night dream, I heard the Buddha’s merit and wisdom being described;
I saw a Dharma Master named Ratnakūṭa, Seated with dignified majesty like the orb of the sun, Expounding the subtle and wondrous scripture of the Golden Light.
At that time, the king awoke from his dream, and great joy arose, pervading his entire body;
when dawn had broken, he departed from the royal palace and went to where the community of bhikṣus resided.
Having paid respectful homage and made offerings to the noble assembly, he immediately questioned that great multitude:
"Is there a Dharma-master named Ratnakūṭa, who has perfected meritorious virtues and transforms sentient beings?"
At that time, the great Dharma Master Ratnākara dwelt within a single room;
with right mindfulness he recited this subtle and wondrous scripture, sitting upright and unmoving, his body and mind in bliss.
At that time, a bhikṣu led the king to the dwelling of Ratnākara;
there he saw him sitting upright within the room, his body suffused with radiant light and wondrous marks.
He said to the King: "This is indeed Ratnakūṭa, who can uphold the profound sphere of the Buddha’s practice;
it is the subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king among all sūtras, the most supreme."
At that time, the king immediately paid homage to Ratnakūṭa; with palms joined in reverence, he made this request:
"I pray only that you, whose full-moon face is so dignified and beautiful, will preach for us the subtle and wondrous Dharma of the Golden Light."
The Dharma Master Ratnakūṭa accepted the King’s invitation and consented to preach this *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*;
throughout the trichiliocosm, the great assemblies of devas were filled with joy.
In a vast, expansive, and pure place, the king adorned it with wondrous and precious jewels;
he sprinkled excellent scented water to settle the dust and scattered various kinds of flowers everywhere.
Thereupon, high seats were arranged in the excellent locations, adorned with suspended silk banners and canopies;
various powdered incenses and unguents were spread, their fragrant scents pervading everywhere.
Devas, nāgas, asuras, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and yakṣas—
all the devas rained down mandārava flowers, coming together to make offerings to that high seat.
Furthermore, there were thousands of millions of devas who, desiring to hear the true Dharma, gathered together;
as soon as the Dharma Master rose from his original seat, they all made offerings to him with celestial flowers.
At that time, the great Dharma Master Ratnakara, having bathed himself clean and donned fresh garments, approached the place where the assembly sat at the Dharma throne;
with palms joined and a reverent heart, he paid his respects.
The Lord of Devas, the hosts of devas, and the celestial maidens all together scattered mandārava flowers;
hundreds of thousands of inconceivable celestial instruments, suspended in the air, produced wondrous sounds.
At that time, the great Dharma Master Ratnākara ascended the high seat and sat cross-legged;
he called to mind all the Buddhas of Great Compassion throughout the hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of lands in the ten directions.
Pervading all sentient beings who suffer, He gives rise to thoughts of impartial compassion;
For the sake of the patron Susambhava, He expounds the subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*.
Having heard such a Dharma as this, the king joined his palms with single-minded devotion and proclaimed his sympathetic joy;
hearing this rare Dharma, his tears flowed freely, and great joy suffused his entire body and mind.
At that time, King Sujāta, the sovereign of the land, in order to make offerings to this sutra,
held in his hand a wish-fulfilling maṇi jewel and made a vow for the sake of all sentient beings.
Now, throughout this Jambudvīpa, may a rain of necklaces and ornaments made of the seven treasures fall everywhere;
may all those who lack wealth and resources obtain whatever they desire and enjoy peace and happiness.
Even if the seven treasures were rained down everywhere, filling all four continents to their full extent;
even if necklaces and ornaments were provided for the body according to every need, and clothing, food, and drink were never lacking.
At that time, King Sujāta, the lord of the land, saw precious jewels raining down upon these four continents;
he took them all to offer as worship to the Buddha Ratnaśikhin and to the community of bhikṣus who upheld his bequeathed teachings.
You should know that the King Suprabuddha of the past was none other than I, Śākyamuni;
because in former times he relinquished the great earth, as well as all the precious treasures filling the four continents.
In former times, the great Dharma Master Ratnakūṭa Expounded the wondrous Dharma for that Sujāta;
Because he revealed and proclaimed this King of Sutras, He has now appeared in the East as Akṣobhya Buddha.
Because I have heard this King of Sutras, I join my palms and utter these words of rejoicing;
Together with the merit of bestowing the seven treasures, I have attained this most supreme adamantine body.
Adorned with the marks of a hundred merits and golden light, all who behold him are filled with joy;
there is no sentient being who does not love him, and the same is true for the millions of celestial hosts.
In the past, throughout ninety-nine koṭis of billions of eons, he served as a wheel-turning monarch;
he also reigned as a human king over small nations for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of eons.
Throughout immeasurable kalpas, he served as Śakra, and likewise once became the Great Brahmā King;
his offerings to the Ten-Powered One of Great Compassion are so numerous that their measure is difficult to exhaust.
In the past, I heard the sutras and rejoiced in their goodness; the measure of the mass of merit therein is difficult to know.
By virtue of this merit, I have realized Bodhi and attained the true, wondrous wisdom of the Dharmakāya.

At that time, having heard these words, the great assembly marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence and all vowed to uphold the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* so that it might circulate without interruption.
