"The Buddha’s body is subtle and wondrous, the color of true gold; Its light shines everywhere, equal to a mountain of gold.
Pure and supple as a lotus flower, Adorned with immeasurable exquisite colors."
Adorned throughout by the thirty-two marks, Fully endowed with all eighty minor characteristics;
His radiance is brilliant and peerless, Stainless like the pure, full moon.

That voice is clear and penetrating, most subtle and wondrous; like the lion’s roar and the sound of thunder, it possesses eight kinds of sublime qualities that respond to the capacities of all beings, surpassing even those of the kalaviṅka and other such birds.
Adorned with the wondrous marks of a hundred blessings, his countenance is majestic; His radiance is complete, pure and stainless;
His wisdom is as clear and bright as the great ocean; His merit is as vast and expansive as space.
The circular halo fills the realms of the ten directions; According to conditions, you universally save all sentient beings.
The afflictions, attachments, and habitual tendencies are all eliminated; The torch of Dharma burns eternally without ceasing.
Out of compassion, you benefit all sentient beings, Able to bestow happiness upon those of the present and the future;
You constantly proclaim the primary truth, Causing them to realize the true tranquility of nirvāṇa.
The Buddha has preached the supreme Dharma of ambrosia, Which can bestow the subtle and wondrous meaning of ambrosia;
It leads one into the city of Nirvāṇa, the ambrosial realm, Causing one to experience the bliss of ambrosial non-action.
Constantly within the great ocean of birth and death, you liberate all sentient beings from suffering;
you cause them to abide upon the path of peace and security, forever bestowing inconceivable, wish-fulfilling bliss.
The ocean of the Tathāgata’s virtues is exceedingly deep and vast, beyond what can be known through any analogy;
toward all beings he constantly gives rise to great compassion, applying skillful means with tireless diligence.
The ocean of the Tathāgata’s wisdom is boundless;
though all humans and devas together attempt to measure it, even in the course of ten million billion kalpas, they could not know even a small fraction of it.
I have now briefly praised the Buddha’s virtues, Which are but a single drop within an ocean of merit;
I dedicate this mass of blessings to all living beings, Praying that they may all swiftly realize the fruit of Bodhi.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"You have skillfully praised the Buddha’s merits in this way; you benefit sentient beings, extensively promote the Buddha's work, can extinguish all transgressions, and generate immeasurable merit."

Chapter 28: The Praise of Bodhisattva Subhūṣaṇadhvaja (10) The Golden Light Most Victorious King Sutra, Chapter Twenty-Eight: The Praise of Bodhisattva Subhūṣaṇadhvaja At that time, Bodhisattva Subhūṣaṇadhvaja rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and spoke this praise:
"The Muni’s marks of a hundred merits are perfect, His body adorned with immeasurable virtues."
Vast and pure, it is a joy for people to behold, Like the radiance of a thousand suns shining forth;
With boundless, blazing hues of flame, It is as majestic in appearance as a mass of exquisite jewels.
Like the sun first rising, reflecting in the void, with red and white clearly distinguished amidst golden hues;
it is also like the light of a mountain of gold shining everywhere, able to pervade hundreds of thousands of lands.
They are able to extinguish the immeasurable sufferings of sentient beings and bestow upon them all boundless, supreme, and wondrous bliss;
endowed with every mark, they are entirely adorned and pure, such that sentient beings never tire of beholding them.
The hair is soft and deep blue-black, like a swarm of black bees gathered upon a wondrous flower;
adorned with the purity of great joy and great equanimity, he is fully endowed with great loving-kindness and great compassion.
Adorned with a multitude of wondrous marks and signs, Accomplished through the factors of enlightenment;
The Tathāgata is able to bestow manifold blessings and benefits, Causing all beings to constantly obtain great peace and happiness.
Adorned together with manifold sublime virtues, His radiance universally illumines ten million lands;
The Tathāgata’s marks of light are perfectly complete, Like the blazing sun pervading the sky.
The Buddha is like Mount Sumeru, complete with all merits, Manifesting his presence throughout the ten directions;
The Tathāgata’s golden mouth is wondrously dignified and beautiful, His teeth white, even, and closely set, like white jade or snow.
The Tathāgata’s countenance is without peer; The tuft of hair between his brows always curls to the right;
Lustrous, fresh, and white as crystal, It is like the full moon dwelling in the expanse of space.
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Wondrous Banner:
“That you are able to praise the Buddha in this way brings inconceivable merit; it benefits all beings and causes those who have not yet known [the truth] to follow and practice accordingly.”

Chapter 29: The Bodhi Tree Deity’s Praise (10). *The Golden Light Most Victorious King Sūtra*, Chapter Twenty-nine: The Bodhi Tree Deity’s Praise. At that time, the Bodhi Tree Deity also praised the World-Honored One with these verses:
"Homage to the Tathāgata of Pure Wisdom!
Homage to the wisdom that constantly seeks the true Dharma!
Homage to the wisdom that is able to depart from what is not the Dharma!
Homage to the wisdom that is eternally free from conceptual discrimination!
How rare, O World-Honored One, are your boundless practices! How rare, as difficult to behold as the udumbara flower!
How rare, like the ocean or the King of Mountains that anchors all! How rare, O Sugata, is your immeasurable light!
How rare is the Great Compassionate Vow of the Tamer! How rare is the Śākya Sage, whose brilliance exceeds that of the sun!
Able to expound such jewels within this sutra, he brings compassion and benefit to all living beings.
The Sage’s faculties are tranquil and stabilized; he is able to enter the city of tranquil nirvāṇa.
He abides in the gateway of tranquil samādhi and can know the profound realm of tranquility.
The Honored One among two-legged beings abides in empty stillness; the bodies of his śrāvaka disciples are likewise empty.
The essential nature of all phenomena is non-existent; all sentient beings are entirely empty and still.
I constantly keep all Buddhas in mind; I always delight in beholding the World-Honored Ones.
I constantly give rise to a heart of earnest devotion, And always encounter the Tathāgata-sun.
I constantly prostrate to the World-Honored One, Vowing that my heart of longing and adoration shall never cease;
With tears of sorrow flowing without interruption, May I always serve you without ever knowing weariness.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will give rise to compassion, And with a serene countenance, allow me always to behold you;
May the Buddha and the assembly of Śrāvakas remain pure, And may they always universally deliver all beings among devas and humans.
The Buddha’s body is fundamentally pure like space, And like a mirage, a flame, or the moon reflected in water;
I pray you will preach the nectar-like Dharma of Nirvāṇa, Which can give birth to the entire mass of all merits.
The pure realm of the World-Honored One, His inconceivable practice of compassion and rectitude—
Is beyond the measure of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, And cannot be fathomed even by great sages and bodhisattvas.
I only pray that the Tathāgata will take pity on me, And always allow me to behold your body of great compassion;
With the three karmas free from weariness, I shall serve the Compassionate Honored One, Swiftly transcending birth and death to return to the limit of reality.
At that time, having heard this praise, the World-Honored One addressed the tree deity with a Brahma-voice, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Good Goddess!

You are able to proclaim the wondrous marks of my true, non-deceptive, and pure Dharmakāya for the benefit of yourself and others. By this merit, may you swiftly realize supreme Bodhi; may all sentient beings practice together with you, and if they hear this, may they all enter the nectar-like Dharma-gate of non-arising."

Chapter 30: The Praise of the Goddess Mahāprajñā (10). From the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, Chapter Thirty: The Praise of the Goddess Mahāprajñā. At that time, the Goddess Mahāprajñā rose from her seat, joined her palms in reverence, and praised the World-Honored One with these straightforward words:
“Homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni!”

His body was the color of pure gold; his throat was like a conch shell; his face was like the full moon; his eyes were like blue lotuses; his lips and mouth were a beautiful red, like the color of crystal; his nose was high, long, and straight, like a polished bar of gold; his teeth were white, even, and closely set, like *kubjaka* flowers; his bodily radiance shone everywhere like a hundred thousand suns; and his luster was clear and penetrating, like the gold of Jambudvīpa.

His speech is free from error; he demonstrates the three gates of liberation and opens the path to the three types of enlightenment. His mind is ever pure, as is his intention; the dwelling place and the sphere of activity of a Buddha are likewise ever pure. He is free from improper conduct, and his movements and pauses are without fault.
Having practiced austerities for six years and turned the Wheel of Dharma three times, he delivers suffering sentient beings, leading them to the further shore.

His physical marks are as perfect as the *kūṭaja* tree; having cultivated the six perfections, his three karmas are without fault. Possessing all-encompassing wisdom, he fulfills the benefit of both self and others. All that he proclaims is always for the sake of sentient beings; his words are never in vain. Among the Śākyas, he is the Great Lion—firm, courageous, and endowed with the eight liberations.

I now praise a small portion of the Tathāgata’s merits according to my capacity, like a mosquito drinking from the waters of the great ocean; by this merit, may it extend widely to all sentient beings, so that they forever leave birth and death behind and achieve the Unsurpassed Way.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Goddess Mahāpratisarā, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"

Having cultivated your practice for a long time and possessing great eloquence, you have now further offered extensive praise to me; may this cause you to swiftly realize the unsurpassed Dharma-gate, with your marks and signs becoming perfectly radiant, so as to universally benefit all beings.

Chapter 31: Entrustment (10). The Golden Light Most Victorious King Sūtra, Chapter Thirty-one: Entrustment. At that time, the World-Honored One addressed all the immeasurable bodhisattvas, as well as the entire great assembly of humans and devas:
“You should know this!”
"Throughout immeasurable and incalculable great eons, I have diligently practiced austerities and attained the profound Dharma, the true cause of Bodhi, which I have already taught to you.
Among you, who can rouse a courageous mind to reverently protect and widely disseminate this Dharma-gate after my parinirvāṇa, so that the True Dharma may long abide in the world?"
At that time, within the assembly, sixty koṭis of great bodhisattvas and sixty koṭis of the great multitude of devas spoke with one voice, saying:
"World-Honored One!

We all possess hearts of joy and delight; for the sake of the profound and subtle Dharma—the true cause of Bodhi—which the Buddha, the World-Honored One, attained through diligent practice and asceticism over immeasurable great kalpas, we shall reverently uphold it, not begrudging even our own bodies or lives.

"After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, you shall widely proclaim and disseminate this Dharma-gate, ensuring that the True Dharma remains long in the world. At that time, the great Bodhisattvas spoke these verses before the Buddha: "The World-Honored One speaks words of truth, Abiding securely in the reality of the Dharma; He has attained the ultimate, supreme path, And is now about to enter parinirvāṇa. The Tathāgata is the Great Physician, Who dispels the darkness of ignorance; Having attained the state of unconditioned peace, He shall forever leave the world behind. We have heard the Buddha’s true words, That he will soon enter parinirvāṇa; Our hearts are filled with grief and sorrow, As we contemplate his departure from the world. May the World-Honored One, out of compassion, Grant us a brief respite from our suffering; May he remain for a while longer, To benefit all sentient beings. Because of that reality, they uphold this sutra;
with great compassion as their armor, they abide in great loving-kindness;
by the power of that compassion, they uphold this sutra.
The provisions of merit being perfected, the provisions of wisdom arise;
because these provisions are fulfilled, one upholds this sutra.
All Māras are subdued, and all false doctrines are destroyed.
Because they have severed evil views, they shall protect and uphold this sutra.
The World Protectors, as well as Śakra and Brahmā, even down to the Asuras;
the Nāgas, spirits, Yakṣas, and others, shall all protect and uphold this sutra.
Those who have long dwelt upon this earth and in the void,
because they uphold the Buddha’s teaching, shall protect and maintain this sutra.
Endowed with the four sublime abodes and adorned by the four noble truths;
Because they have subdued the four māras, they protect and uphold this sutra.
Even if empty space were to become solid matter, or solid matter were to become empty space,
those whom the Buddhas protect and uphold cannot be shaken or moved.

At that time, when the Four Great Heavenly Kings heard the Buddha speak of this protection and upholding of the sublime Dharma, each gave rise to a mind of sympathetic joy and a resolve to protect the True Dharma. Simultaneously, with one voice, they spoke these verses:
"We now, regarding this sutra, And its male and female followers;
With single-minded devotion shall we protect and uphold it, Causing it to be widely circulated."
"If there be those who uphold this sutra, they shall be able to create the cause for Bodhi;
I shall always, from the four directions, protect and serve them.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, joined his palms in reverence and spoke these verses:
"The Buddhas have realized this Dharma; desiring to repay their debt of gratitude, they appear in the world to preach this sutra for the benefit of the assembly of Bodhisattvas.
Toward those Buddhas, I shall always make offerings to repay their kindness."
"Protect and uphold such a sutra, as well as those who uphold the sutra.
At that time, the devaputra Tuṣita joined his palms in reverence and spoke this verse:
"If there are those who can uphold such a sutra as spoken by the Buddha;"
When I abide in the stage of Bodhi, I shall be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven.
O World-Honored One, I am filled with joy;
having relinquished my sublime celestial retribution, I shall dwell in Jambudvīpa and proclaim this sūtra.
At that time, Brahmā Śikhin, the lord of the Sahā world, joined his palms in reverent salutation and spoke these verses:
"All meditative concentrations and immeasurables, All vehicles and liberations— They all emerge from this sutra; Therefore, I proclaim this sutra."
"Wherever this sutra is preached, I shall renounce the pleasures of the Brahma Heaven;
for the sake of hearing such a sutra, I shall also constantly provide protection.
At that time, the Māra prince named Śreṣṭhidāraka joined his palms in reverence and spoke these verses:
"If there be those who receive and uphold this sutra, which accords with the true Dharma,
they shall not follow the ways of Māra, but shall purify the evil karma of Māra.
We, too, shall diligently protect this sutra."
"Arousing the mind of great diligence, may it be widely circulated everywhere.
At that time, Māra joined his palms in reverence and spoke these verses:
"If there are those who uphold this sutra, they will be able to subdue all afflictions."
In this way, for all such classes of sentient beings, I shall provide protection so that they may dwell in peace and happiness.
If there be anyone who recites this sutra, no māras shall find an opportunity against them;
by virtue of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, I shall protect them.
At that time, the divine son Mañjuśrī also spoke a verse before the Buddha, saying:
"The wondrous enlightenment of all Buddhas Is expounded within this sutra;
Whoever upholds this sutra Is making offerings to the Tathāgata."
"I shall uphold this sutra and preach it for ten million devas;
to those who listen with reverence, I shall exhort them toward the state of Bodhi.
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva joined his palms in reverent salutation and spoke these verses:
"If I see one who abides in Bodhi, I shall act as their uninvited friend;
even at the cost of my own body and life, I shall protect this King of Sutras.
Having heard such a Dharma as this, I shall go to the Tuṣita Heaven."
"By the grace of the Blessed One, it shall be extensively taught for the sake of humans and devas.
At that time, the Elder Mahākāśyapa joined his palms in reverence and spoke these verses:
"Regarding the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Buddha said that my wisdom is meager;"
Now, according to my own power, I shall protect and uphold such a sūtra as this.
If there be anyone who holds this sūtra, I shall receive and support them;
I shall grant them the power of eloquence and always follow them, praising: "Excellent!"
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda joined his palms toward the Buddha and spoke these verses:
"I have personally heard from the Buddha Countless sūtras and discourses;
Yet never before have I heard such a thing— The King of all profound and wondrous Dharmas."
"Having now heard this sutra, I have received it personally before the Buddha;
those who delight in Bodhi should widely proclaim and disseminate it.

At that time, the World-Honored One, seeing that the great assembly of bodhisattvas, humans, and devas had each resolved their minds to circulate and protect this scripture, and encouraging the bodhisattvas to extensively benefit sentient beings, spoke in praise:
“Excellent! Excellent!

That you are able to reverently propagate such a subtle and wondrous king of sutras, even unto after my parinirvāṇa so that it does not perish, is the true cause for unsurpassed bodhi; the merit thereby obtained could not be fully described even in kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.”

If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or other sons and daughters of good family who make offerings and show reverence, transcribe and circulate it, and explain it for others, the merit they obtain will likewise be such as this; therefore, you all should diligently practice and cultivate it.

At that time, the immeasurable and boundless great assembly, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.

This tenth fascicle of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-uttamarāja-sūtra* was based on a Sanskrit manuscript preserved in the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain; compared with other versions intended for translation, it contains many omissions, particularly regarding the *dhāraṇīs*, which are frequently absent.
This edition was produced by collating it with the Tibetan translation held in the library of the Sino-Tibetan Studies Institute.
For there are two versions of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* in the Tibetan canon; one is indeed the original Chinese version translated by Yi Jing, and its close correspondence is only natural.
Nevertheless, where minor discrepancies occur, they shall be evident to the reader.
The Tathāgata Nirvāṇahulakadhvajavyākaraṇananda-śrīguṇasāgara.
